text:
alex: heads-up — seeing ~8-12% p95/p99 tail latency bump on SM90s after the new Triton->auto kernel selector landed this morning :thinking_face:
cheng: ack, saw the alert. any traces? is it steady or only for certain seq/batch mixes?
sam: looks worst for mixed small-batch + long-seq chat workloads (batch 1-4, seq 2k+). stable repro on a DL1 instance we used for nightly.
maria: can you paste the profiling snippet? curious if it's an attn kernel switch or memcpy hotpath.
alex: here's a short perf trace from the failing run (trimmed):
```
# trace excerpt (nvprof-like)
SM90 instance: model=redwood-v1-fused, batch=2, seq=2048
2026-03-17T08:12:02.123Z  cudaMemcpyAsync HtoD  1.2ms
2026-03-17T08:12:02.126Z  TritonKernel flash_attn_variant_a  6.9ms
2026-03-17T08:12:02.133Z  TritonKernel flash_attn_variant_b  9.8ms
2026-03-17T08:12:02.143Z  cudaMemcpyAsync DtoH  0.9ms
```
cheng: interesting — two different Triton kernels invoked back-to-back (variant_a then variant_b). that smells like selector oscillation when seq distribution crosses a threshold.
sam: i repro locally if i force selector to prefer `cuda_fused` instead of `triton_flash_v2` — latency drops ~10%.
maria: could paged KV behavior be interacting? switch between kernels might cause extra KV materialization / cache miss and memcpy churn.
devprof: added some flamegraph diff output to the ticket — top-level shows extra kernel launch overhead + stalling on stream synchronization when fallback happens.
infra-bot: nightly-compare (1925552000 -> 1925554000): eng-runtime/flash-attn-sm90: p95 +9.8%, p99 +11.4%, CPU CPU_sys +3.2%
alex: hypothesis: new heuristic used Triton kernels for medium-length keys but for tail seqs we fall back to a slightly different variant which doesn't reuse prefetched KV layout, so we pay memcpy + kernel re-init.
cheng: agree. i dug into selector code — it uses a per-request micro-benchmark that picks top-2 kernels then probes expected latency. the probe code has a bug when batch<4 where it incorrectly estimates kernel B as faster and triggers a second kernel.
sam: quick mitigation: add a guard to avoid switching kernels mid-request if KV layout already populated. i can prototype a toggle in runtime config.
maria: also file: we should add a workload-aware batching heuristic: for chat workloads with high seq variance, prefer stable kernel even if slightly slower on median. reduces tail regressions.
alex: can you sketch the runtime flag? something like `kernel_selector.allow_midreq_switch=false`?
devprof: proposed config snippet below — i tested it on staging, p95 improved and median unchanged:
```
{
  "kernel_selector": {
    "mode": "stable",
    "allow_midreq_switch": false,
    "stable_preference": ["cuda_fused","triton_flash_v2"]
  }
}
```
cheng: that aligns. i'll prepare a PR to bump the selector and add a unit test that simulates KV warm/cold transitions.
maria: we should also run a cross-arch microbenchmark matrix: SM80/SM86/SM90 x CUDA12.1/12.2 x Triton 2.20/2.22. differences are subtle — kernel launch cost differs on SM90 for small kernels.
sam: noted. i'll enqueue jobs on cluster: label `kernel-portability/selector-regress` and run overnight across regions. will share results.
alex: product note — inform SRE that we plan a hotfix toggle on prod if we see customer impact.
infra-bot: job queued: kernel-portability/selector-regress (6 configs) -> started run 1925554400.
cheng: one more thing — KV paged attention path does an extra pointer indirection when switching variants; add a fastpath to reuse the same page table across compatible kernels. that should eliminate memcpy thrash.
maria: agree, but need to be careful with alignment and quantized layouts. add integration tests for same-model different-kernel execution.
devprof: adding a perf regression alert on release branch to detect >5% p95 delta on mixed chat workloads.
alex: thanks everyone. next steps: (1) sam runs matrix and posts results, (2) cheng PR to selector guard + test, (3) devprof add alert + config toggle. we'll reconvene after jobs finish. :thumbsup: 
sam: on it — i'll paste the matrix link once done.
cheng: drafting PR now.
maria: will prep integration tests for KV fastpath.
infra-bot: run complete: kernel-portability/selector-regress -> summary: SM90+Triton2.22 still shows +8% p95 when selector=auto, mitigation `stable` reduces to +1.5%. full logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1925554400/logs
alex: great, closing the loop. let's land the selector guard and add the KV fastpath task to the sprint.
